labels.text: Bug report sent to the AGI Workforce team. Thank you.

S88.04.needs: an account that can reach the AGI server (the report is posted to the server)
S88.04.note: The code sends the version and platform, but the tester cannot see that it is stored for the team; only the confirmation line is shown.
steps: Start the CLI with agi and wait for the chat prompt.
Type /bug alone and press Enter; read the usage text that appears.
Type /bug the diff view hangs on large files and press Enter.
Look for the line Bug report sent to the AGI Workforce team. Thank you. Compare with Expected: the usage text says the report carries the CLI version and platform.
S88.04.where: In the chat, type /bug and press Enter (usage text), then type /bug <description> (for example /bug the diff view hangs on large files)

labels.text: Write a redacted diagnostics file to review and attach to a support request.
Read it before you attach it to a support request; it holds only what is listed above.

S88.07.needs: a signed-in account (the export is posted to the AGI server)
S88.07.note: No in-product choice to share with support exists in the code; the file is only written to the current folder.
steps: Run agi doctor --export in the folder where you want the file.
Read the printed summary above the Wrote line.
Find the Wrote <file>.json line; open that JSON file and check it holds only what the printed report lists.
Compare with Expected: the file is written, but the CLI has no prompt to share it; the user attaches it to support by hand.
S88.07.where: In a terminal, run agi doctor --export

S88.08.needs: a way to make a request fail, such as an expired sign-in or a model that rejects the request
S88.08.note: The id appears only when the failure carries a request id, so it is not shown for every error; the trigger is not in the code.
steps: Start agi and send a message that makes the provider return an error (the code does not name a fixed trigger).
Read the error text under the failed turn.
Look for a line Reference: <id>. Compare with Expected: the id is shown only when the failure carries one.
S88.08.where: In the chat, send a message whose request fails; the error text shows a line that starts with Reference:

S88.13.needs: an older CLI build than the latest release, so a newer release is available
S88.13.note: The What's new notice is shown once per version, and only when the release has notes.
steps: Run an older build of agi, then update to a newer release (or use a build older than the latest release).
Start agi and read the start screen for the What's new line and the Release notes: link.
In the chat, type /changelog and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the release notes are shown from inside the product.
S88.13.where: Start agi after an update and read the start screen for What's new; or in the chat type /changelog

S88.14.needs: none; a deprecated model appears only when the catalog has one, which a tester cannot choose
S88.14.note: No replacement is named in the code for a retiring model; the code only shows the retirement date and a deprecated flag, and the picker line is deprecated, leaves <date>.
steps: Type agi models list and press Enter.
Find any model marked with ! and read its line deprecated, leaves the catalog <date> if one shows.
In the chat, type /model and press Enter; move to a model and read the detail line under the list (deprecated, leaves <date>).
Compare with Expected: a warning before retirement is shown, but no replacement model name is shown in these places.
S88.14.where: In a terminal, type agi models list; in the chat, type /model and move to a model

labels.text: Migrate settings from another coding CLI. Defaults to Claude Code.

S88.15.needs: a Claude Code setup in ~/.claude (for example an mcp.json file) to import from
S88.15.note: The only migration source in the code is Claude Code; the chat has no /migrate command in the TUI, and the replaced-feature case is not covered.
steps: Run agi migrate --dry-run and read the output that starts with Claude Code migration dry run.
Check the MCP line (added, already present) and the Source line in the preview.
Run agi migrate (without --dry-run) and read Claude Code migration complete.
Compare with Expected: the preview comes before any change is written.
S88.15.where: In a terminal, run agi migrate --dry-run, then agi migrate
